subject.title: macOS launchd Gateway still restarts via gateway-update/update.run; document and honor auto-update kill-switch

question: Should `OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1` suppress supervised Gateway control-plane `update.run` managed-service handoffs, or should it remain limited to configured background auto-update applies?
rationale: The current env var is documented and tested as a background-auto-update kill-switch, while broadening it to explicit/control-plane update requests changes a public operator contract on a high-risk update/restart path.

options.title: Honor it for supervised update.run
options.body: Treat the env as a headless-operator hard stop for Gateway package/restart handoffs, return a clear skipped/refused result, and add docs plus focused tests for the new scope.

options.title: Keep background-only scope
options.body: Leave explicit `update.run` runnable, document the env as background-only, and keep availability fixes on the macOS launchd update.run tracker.

options.title: Define a separate hard-stop knob
options.body: Add a new documented policy only if maintainers want a distinct control-plane update kill-switch instead of overloading the existing env var.

recommendation.title: Honor it for supervised update.run
recommendation.body: Treat the env as a headless-operator hard stop for Gateway package/restart handoffs, return a clear skipped/refused result, and add docs plus focused tests for the new scope.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing kill-switch and have recent adjacent update lifecycle history, making them the best available owner for the scope decision.
